items.title: Janakpur bowlers restrict Karnali to 132
items.desc: Captain Harmeet Singh takes three wickets as Karnali Yaks lose nine wickets in their 20 overs in the Nepal Premier League.

items.title: Kathmandu Valley to consume 5.18 million flower garlands this Tihar
items.desc: Domestic growers are expected to meet nearly 89 percent of demand as the festival’s flower trade, including plants and potted chrysanthemums, approaches Rs645 million.

items.title: Nepali lawmaker faces privacy backlash over videos of children filmed with smart glasses
items.desc: Ashika Tamang blurred a child’s face after criticism, but rights advocates say her videos raise wider questions about consent and the responsibilities of elected representatives.

items.title: Budhigandaki needs commitment, not another new plan
items.desc: Repeated shifts in financing and implementation have delayed Nepal’s largest reservoir project.

items.title: Who does Nepal Police serve?
items.desc: Is police power guided by law, evidence and accountable command, or by obedience to whoever happens to hold power?

items.title: Attackers kill 60 people in Ethiopia’s conflict-hit Oromiya region, Orthodox church says
items.desc: The ​Holy Synod of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church said ​14 believers were killed in Merti Woreda on October 20 and 46 in Sherka Woreda on October 24.

items.title: Drones came after Lirung. Nepal needs them before the next collapse
items.desc: In Nepal, researchers still need permission for each project to use drones that monitor dangerous slopes before they fail.

items.title: Fastest turnout in 45 years as Israelis pass wartime judgment on Netanyahu
items.desc: The Central Elections Committee reported that 16.7 percent of eligible voters had already cast their ballots within the first three hours, the fastest early turnout rate since 1981.

items.title: Handigaun Jatra: A jatra like no other
items.desc: Handigaun’s three-day festival features upside-down chariot spires, wax flowers and a legend about a woman who endured 12 years of labour.

items.title: Chitwan Rhinos defeat Biratnagar Kings by eight runs
items.desc: Kamal Singh Airee took four wickets as Biratnagar fell short of a 158-run target despite Andre Russell’s late 33 off 17 balls.

items.title: The NPL is on, but fans in Achham can’t get a signal
items.desc: As the tournament unfolds in Kathmandu, supporters in remote villages are travelling to nearby settlements and market centres to watch their teams.

items.title: Nepal gives 35 days to agency owners yet to respond to arrest warrants
items.desc: The Department of Foreign Employment warns of banking and travel restrictions for those who fail to report, as it investigates Malaysia’s selection of 25 Nepali recruitment agencies.

items.title: Biratnagar Kings need 158 to win
items.desc: Losing the toss and batting first, Chitwan Rhinos managed 157/3 in the first innings on the back of Dawid Malan’s 70 off 50.

items.title: How Pakistan’s NOC rules are affecting the Nepal Premier League
items.desc: A reported $25,000 clearance demand has disrupted team plans, leaving franchises uncertain about the availability of seven Pakistani players signed for the tournament.

items.title: Nepalis in Saudi Arabia urged to follow security alerts amid drone attacks
items.desc: The embassy in Riyadh calls for vigilance and warns against sharing unverified reports as missile and drone threats persist.

items.title: Nepal’s historic loss and damage allocation falls short of its needs
items.desc: The UN fund has provisionally set aside 21.6 million for Nepal after the Rasuwa disaster, marking a first while covering less than 0.5 percent of the country’s estimated $4.7 billion recovery and reconstruction needs.
